mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about prime numbers is FALSE?

options.A: A prime number has exactly two distinct positive divisors.
options.B: 2 is the only even prime number.
options.C: 1 is a prime number because it has only one divisor.
options.D: Every prime number greater than 2 is odd.

mcqs.answer: 1 is a prime number because it has only one divisor.
mcqs.explanation: A prime number is defined as a natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and itself. The number 1 has only one divisor (itself), so it does not meet the definition of a prime. Therefore option C is the false statement. Options A, B, and D correctly describe properties of prime numbers.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines a composite number?

options.A: A number that has exactly one positive divisor.
options.B: A number that can be expressed as the product of two natural numbers greater than 1.
options.C: A number that is divisible only by itself.

mcqs.answer: A number that can be expressed as the product of two natural numbers greater than 1.
mcqs.explanation: A composite number is a natural number greater than 1 that has more than two positive divisors, meaning it can be written as a product of two integers each larger than 1. Option B captures this definition. Option A describes the number 1, option C describes prime numbers, and option D is incorrect because primes are not composite.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly identifies the first number as prime and the second as composite?
mcqs.explanation: 11 has only the divisors 1 and 11, so it is prime. 15 can be divided by 1, 3, 5, and 15, so it is composite. Hence option A correctly classifies the first number as prime and the second as composite. In option B, 9 is composite and 13 is prime (reversed). Option C has 14 composite and 17 prime (reversed). Option D has 21 composite and 23 prime (reversed).

mcqs.question: In the classification of natural numbers as prime or composite, which statement about the number 1 is true?

options.A: 1 is considered a composite number because it has more than one factor.
options.B: 1 is neither prime nor composite because it has only one positive divisor.
options.C: 1 is a prime number because it is only divisible by itself.

mcqs.answer: 1 is neither prime nor composite because it has only one positive divisor.
mcqs.explanation: The number 1 has exactly one positive divisor (itself). By definition, a prime number must have exactly two distinct positive divisors, and a composite number must have more than two. Since 1 meets neither condition, it is classified as neither prime nor composite. Options A, C, and D incorrectly assign 1 to one of the two categories.
